To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
our Palaeolithic ancestors evolved in a land– water ecosystem and extracted a considerable part of their diets both from land and water.
the diet of our ancestors included aquatic resources, which were a substantial part of the diet, and that this diet is beneficial to health.
the Palaeolithic diet is the only dietary regimen that is consistent with the evolutionary characteristics of our species.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a multidisciplinary reconstruction and evaluation of Palaeolithic diets, which hold promise for the prevention of chronic degenerative diseases.
the reconstruction of Palaeo-diet, which has implications for the prevention and management of diseases of civilisations.
the reconstruction of the Palaeolithic environment and diet and their implications for health and disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the diet of Palaeolithic hominins was rich in aquatic and terrestrial resources.
our ancestors were aquatic, and that their diet was rich in aquatic resources.
the human species evolved in the vicinity of water and consumed aquatic and terrestrial resources.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ‘Palaeolithic’ diet is a ‘healthy’ diet.
our ancestors lived on a diet that consisted of a wide range of both aquatic and terrestrial foods.
our ancestors were not ‘cave-men’ but lived in the proximity of the water, which was the basis for a healthy diet.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a Palaeolithic diet is a healthy diet.

a diet based on the consumption of a wide range of terrestrial and aquatic resources, including wild plants, wild animals, insects, eggs, fish, shellfish and marine invertebrates, is the most likely to have provided our ancestors with the nutrients required for health and survival.
the Palaeolithic diet, which is based on the assumption of a land–water ecological niche, holds promise for the treatment and prevention of chronic diseases of civilisation.
